papers.ai_note: 范围综述而非系统评价/Meta分析，纳入的均为病例报告与小病例系列，无对照组，无法估计疗效；'无严重不良事件'仅基于5项病例报告的报告偏倚数据，信息不足以外推安全性；'18例肺部'与总数20例存在2例外部病例归类未说明；结局采用'一过性改善/培养转阴'等非标准化定义，摘要未给出具体应答率、培养转阴比例或随访时长，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) comprise a diverse group of organisms that can cause pulmonary and extrapulmonary disease. Their management is challenging, because many NTM species exhibit intrinsic antimicrobial resistance; current multidrug treatment regimens have limited efficacy and tolerability; and the number of immunocompromised individuals at risk of NTM disease is increasing. Phage therapy has recently emerged as a potential therapeutic option for refractory NTM pulmonary disease (NTM-PD). This scoping review aimed to map and critically assess the existing evidence on the clinical use of phage therapy for NTM-PD and its reported outcomes. METHODS: PubMed, SCOPUS, Web of Science and Embase were searched for studies published between August 2015 and August 2025, in any language, addressing phage therapy in NTM-PD. Additional backward and forward citation searches were conducted to identify further relevant studies. RESULTS: Five studies met the inclusion criteria: four single-patient case reports and one small case series representing 20 unique patients treated with phage therapy. Of these, 18 had pulmonary NTM disease, mostly involving drug-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus infections treated under compassionate-use protocols or individualised regimens. Reported clinical and microbiological outcomes were inconsistent: some patients showed transient improvement or culture conversion, while others had no measurable benefit. Phage resistance was uncommon but incompletely assessed, and immune-mediated neutralisation emerged as a future concern. No serious adverse events were described. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports the feasibility but not the efficacy of phage therapy for NTM-PD. Published data are limited to isolated, heterogeneous cases and lack standardised definitions or controlled comparisons. Well-designed, prospective clinical trials are needed to clarify its therapeutic potential and optimise future application.

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：亚型与28天死亡的主要比较仅以'无显著关联'表述，未给出效应量、95%CI与P值，无法评估效能与等效性，'no evidence of increased risk'不等于已证实无差异（可能存在效能不足）。2025-2026季亚型结果仅覆盖265/366例，且K亚分支证据仅来自40例测序样本，选择性缺失可能引入偏倚。摘要未报告28天总体死亡率及各亚型死亡人数，主要终点的绝对风险缺失。系统发育'无按严重程度聚集'的判据与统计方法未说明。观察性设计，混杂（疫苗接种、基础病、治疗差异）未在摘要中交代
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intense influenza activity has been reported alongside the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. While epidemiological studies have reported heterogeneous findings regarding public health impact, data remain lacking on its impact on clinical phenotype of people requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. METHODS: Prospective, multicenter, observational SEVARVIR cohort study including people admitted in 42 French ICUs with laboratory-confirmed influenza infection during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Primary end point was day-28 mortality. RESULTS: Seven hundred twenty-six people were admitted for influenza in 2024-2025 (n = 360) and 2025-2026 (n = 366). In 2025-2026, influenza subtype was available for 265 people; 49% (n = 129) had A(H1N1)pdm09 and 51% (n = 136) had A(H3N2) subtype infection. Among the 40 people with A(H3N2) infection for whom whole-genome sequencing was available, 33 (82.5%) belonged to subclade K. In multivariable Cox analysis of the 2025-2026 season, age (adjusted hazard ratio, aHR = 1.04 [1.01;1.09]; P = .015), Clinical Frailty Scale (aHR = 1.59 [1.28;1.98]; P < .001), and sequential organ failure assessment score (aHR = 1.15 [1.05;1.26]; P = .003) were associated with an increased risk of death. In the 2024-2025/2025-2026 seasons or 2025-2026 season alone, influenza subtype was not associated with a significant risk of day-28 mortality. Phylogenetic analyses from our ICU cohort together with 600 contextual sequences from community-acquired influenza cases collected during the period showed no clustering according to severity. CONCLUSIONS: There was no evidence of an increased risk of death among critically ill people with influenza during the 2025-2026 season, despite the emergence of influenza A(H3N2) subclade K. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05162508.

papers.title_zh: 以住院期间末次PaCO2预测COPD急性加重出院后3个月持续性高碳酸血症：训练队列n=69、AUC 0.779的预测模型研究
papers.title_en: Hospitalization Data for a Severe Acute Exacerbation of COPD as Predictors for Persistent Hypercapnia at 3 Months After Discharge.
papers.authors: Archontakis-Barakakis P, Brownlee CM, Hazenberg A, Wijkstra PJ, Fortis S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Hospital Medicine, Beth Israel Lahey Health - Beverly Hospital, Beverly, MA, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: The last inpatient PaCO2 measurement may help predict persistent hypercapnia 3 months after discharge.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：研究目的称进行了外部验证并纳入年龄与既往住院史建模，但摘要仅报告训练集的AUC与分层发生率，验证队列结果及含年龄/住院史模型表现完全缺失，无法判断模型泛化能力；训练样本仅69例、事件数有限，AUC的CI下限0.667提示精度不足；未给校准度、决策曲线等预测模型必备评价指标；以训练集自身AUC报告存在乐观偏倚风险；分层发生率的P<0.001为趋势检验，摘要未说明检验方法
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This study's purpose was to develop a prognostication model to predict persistent hypercapnia 3 months after discharge in patients hospitalized for COPD exacerbation and hypercapnia. METHODS: We developed the prediction model using a training data set comprising of participants in the RESCUE trial who received no ventilation support at home. We externally validated the model with a retrospective cohort. We calculated the rate of persistent hypercapnia 3 months post hospitalization according to the inpatient PaCO2. We also built regression models that included age and prior hospitalizations and calculated Area Under Curve (AUC). RESULTS: Our training cohort consisted of 69 participants. Among participants with baseline PaCO2 levels between 45 and 52mmHg, 59% had persistent hypercapnia at 3 months. It increased to 73.1% with PaCO2 between 53 and 60mmHg and 100% with greater than 60 mmHg (P < 0.001). Our regression model showed that for each one mmHg increase in baseline PaCO2 the 3-month PaCO2 increased by 0.41. The AUC was 0.779 (95%CI of 0.667 to 0.891). CONCLUSION: The last inpatient PaCO2 measurement may help predict persistent hypercapnia 3 months after discharge.

papers.title_zh: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters.
papers.title_en: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters.
papers.authors: Arroyave A, Rabezanahary H, Sahli A, Baz M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Infectious and Immune Diseases, CHU de Québec Research Center, Québec, Québec, Canada.
papers.abstract_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters. While normal hamsters showed no mortality and achieved viral clearance, infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. In the antiviral efficacy experiment, placebo-treated hamsters exhibited 50% mortality. Baloxavir resulted in 100% survival, shortened viral shedding, reduced viral replication and pulmonary inflammatory responses, and prevented neuroinvasion. High-dose molnupiravir also prevented mortality and achieved viral clearance in lung and brain tissues. Combination therapy resulted in 75% survival and similarly achieved viral clearance in both tissues, with reduced morbidity compared with oseltamivir and low-dose molnupiravir monotherapies. Oseltamivir resulted in 75% survival but failed to prevent severe clinical signs or reduce tissue viral titers, whereas low-dose molnupiravir showed outcomes comparable to placebo. These findings demonstrate the high pathogenicity of a human A(H5N1) isolate in immunosuppressed hamsters, support baloxavir as an effective therapeutic option, and identify molnupiravir-based regimens as promising strategies for severe influenza A(H5N1) infection.

papers.title_zh: 奥希替尼耐药患者来源模型中CD44阳性耐药态与CD44阴性敏感态并存，表型异质性而非持续EGFR信号与耐药相关

papers.authors: Chillico IC, Frascino M, Protopapa G, Ruzzi F, Nironi E, Giunchi F, Pistone D, Gruppioni E et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Molecular Medicine, University of Pavia, Pavia, Italy.
papers.authors_conclusion: LIBM-ADK-11是一个临床相关的奥希替尼耐药EGFR突变NSCLC模型，其中CD44阳性药物耐受态与CD44阴性药物敏感态并存；这些发现突出表型异质性作为奥希替尼耐药的潜在决定因素，并支持在疾病进展时针对不同细胞状态的治疗策略
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：耐药与敏感的判定为定性描述，摘要无IC50、耐药倍数或统计学数值支撑；单患者来源模型，样本量n=1，结论外推至患者群体的证据有限；'P2耐药'仅以生长抑制程度定性表述，缺乏量化药效终点；无体内验证；数值未经四元组核验
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is a standard first-line treatment for EGFR-mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance remains a clinical challenge. Resistance involves genetic mechanisms and non-genetic cell-state transitions, including epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) plasticity and drug-tolerant persister phenotypes. Patient-derived models established at disease progression may better capture clinically relevant resistance mechanisms. METHODS: We established LIBM-ADK-11 from the pleural effusion of a patient with EGFR exon 19p.Leu747_Pro753delinsSer-mutant NSCLC progressing on osimertinib. Cells were studied at low and high passages and fractionated by CD44 expression into CD44-positive/P2 and CD44-negative/P4 subpopulations. EGFR mutation status, CD44 expression, transcriptomics, growth, osimertinib sensitivity, EGFR signaling, sphere formation, cell-cycle distribution and pemetrexed response were evaluated. RESULTS: LIBM-ADK-11 retained the EGFR mutation during long-term culture. CD44 sorting identified two phenotypically distinct cell states. CD44-positive P2 cells were enriched for extracellular matrix remodeling, EMT-like, inflammatory, CAF-like and macrophage/TAM-mimicry programs, with increased glycolysis-related signatures, slower growth, higher metabolic activity and osimertinib resistance. CD44-negative P4 cells displayed a more epithelial profile, cholesterol-associated gene expression and greater osimertinib sensitivity. Osimertinib inhibited EGFR phosphorylation in both populations, indicating that P2 resistance was not explained by persistent EGFR signaling. Long-term culture favored loss of CD44-positive cells, whereas osimertinib delayed this loss and preferentially depleted the CD44-negative fraction. Pemetrexed partially reduced both compartments. CONCLUSIONS: LIBM-ADK-11 is a clinically relevant model of osimertinib-resistant EGFR-mutant NSCLC in which CD44-positive drug-tolerant and CD44-negative drug-sensitive states coexist. These findings highlight phenotypic heterogeneity as a potential determinant of osimertinib resistance and support strategies addressing distinct cellular states at disease progression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Peak inspiratory flow (PIF) is a critical determinant of dry powder inhaler (DPI) effectiveness in managing patients with COPD. Suboptimal PIF may compromise drug delivery and clinical outcomes. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the association between repeated PIF measures and disease exacerbations, hospitalisations, and symptom burden in patients with stable COPD. METHODS: In this multi-country, observational cohort, 415 participants aged ≥40 years with confirmed COPD and a smoking history underwent PIF measurements at their prescribed inhaler's resistance, and low- and high-resistance levels using the In-Check DIAL G16. Clinical assessments occurred at 3 months (follow-up 1 (FU1)) and 6 months (follow-up 2 (FU2)) including spirometry, COPD Assessment Test scores, medication use and exacerbation/hospitalisation rates. RESULTS: At FU1, 29.4% (n=113/384) had typical suboptimal PIF and 28.6% (n=108/377) remained suboptimal at FU2. Participants with suboptimal PIF were more often female and current smokers, with consistently poorer lung function across both visits. Lower forced expiratory volume in 1 s (33.7±9.1% pred versus 45.7±9.2% pred, p=0.01), actual forced vital capacity and inspiratory capacity were observed. Suboptimal PIF significantly predicted moderate (p=0.03) and severe (p=0.01) exacerbations, was associated with higher hospitalisation risks (p=0.05) and with greater use of short-acting beta agonist, oral corticosteroid and triple therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Suboptimal PIF is a stable, clinically meaningful marker of worse COPD outcomes and may guide more personalised inhaler selection.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Malignant pleural effusions (MPE) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are common and generally associated with a poor prognosis. Numerous studies have highlighted improved outcomes for NSCLC patients treated with targeted therapies, however these studies often utilize heterogenous populations of metastatic NSCLC. Our aim was to assess the overall survival of NSCLC patients with MPE and actionable biomarkers. METHODS: We reviewed patients with MPE related to lung cancer managed with indwelling tunneled pleural catheter (IPC) between 2008-2020. Demographics and advanced molecular testing results were reviewed to determine the presence of actionable biomarkers (EGFR=Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor, ALK=Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase, ROS=ROS Proto-Oncogene 1, PDL1=Programmed Death Ligand). Kaplan-Meier testing comparing overall survival per molecular testing results (positive/negative) was performed. RESULTS: A total of 129 patients with NSCLC and MPE undergoing IPC placement were identified. The median age was 70 (IQR - 61.5-80) years with a median survival of 87 (IQR - 32-266.5) days from IPC placement. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated no significant association between molecular marker testing status (positive/negative) and overall survival (EGFR, p=0.70, ALK, p=0.50, ROS1, p=0.40, and PD-L1, p=0.40). CONCLUSION: Within a population of patients undergoing IPC placement for MPE management, the presence of targetable biomarkers was not associated with improved survival when compared to patients that did not have a targetable biomarker. Additional research is needed to explore the associations between outcomes in NSCLC patients with MPE and the presence of targetable biomarkers.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

papers.abstract_en: Digital health is increasingly embedded in cystic fibrosis (CF) care, spanning telehealth, mobile applications, remote monitoring, sensors, and data-driven decision support. Despite this rapid growth, CF digital health research remains fragmented, characterised by inconsistent terminology, disciplinary silos, and challenges in translating innovations into routine clinical practice. Many digital health technologies (DHTs) remain confined to small-scale pilots, while technological capability continues to outpace evaluation methodologies. This review applies the "eHealth evaluation cycle" as a structured framework to examine CF digital health research across the full development-to-implementation pathway. By mapping representative CF studies to the stages of conceptualisation, design and usability, feasibility, effectiveness, and implementation, the review highlights both strengths and gaps in the current evidence base. CF digital health research demonstrates notable maturity at the effectiveness stage, with several high-quality trials, but remains comparatively underdeveloped in early conceptual planning and late-stage implementation research. Adopting a life-cycle lens clarifies how evaluation methods should align with intervention maturity and supports more efficient and safer progression of DHTs. Moving forward, CF digital health research must prioritise structured early-phase development, rigorous feasibility work, and dedicated implementation studies to enable sustainable integration into clinical care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The airway microbiome and host inflammatory response synergistically drive cystic fibrosis (CF) lung disease. We hypothesized that integrating airway microbial community structures with inflammatory biomarker profiles would reveal distinct ecological-inflammatory endotypes associated with clinical outcome measures. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional secondary analysis of 112 clinically stable people with CF. Baseline sputum microbial communities were profiled via 16S rRNA sequencing, clustered using partitioning around medoids and linked with previously quantified inflammatory biomarker data. Co-occurrence network analyses assessed microbial community organisation. Associations with time-to-next pulmonary exacerbation (PEx) and 5-year prognostic survival scores were evaluated utilizing Cox proportional hazards models and multivariable regression. RESULTS: Two distinct ecological-inflammatory endotypes were identified. Endotype 1 (n = 65) exhibited higher microbial diversity, enrichment of oral-associated commensals (e.g., Prevotella, Veillonella), a highly interconnected co-occurrence network, and a moderated inflammatory milieu. Endotype 2 (n = 47) was characterized by Pseudomonas dominance, elevated neutrophilic inflammation (e.g., neutrophil elastase, IL-1β), and more advanced lung disease. The two-cluster solution was highly stable under repeated subsampling. Higher microbial diversity was independently associated with a more favourable 5-year prognostic survival score, including after adjustment for endotype membership. Endotype membership itself was not associated with time to subsequent PEx, and associations between ecological measures and PEx were attenuated after additional adjustment for baseline lung function. CONCLUSIONS: Distinct ecological-inflammatory endotypes in the CF airway reflect differences in microbial community structure, inflammatory state and underlying disease severity. Longitudinal studies are required to determine the stability of these states and their relationship with subsequent clinical disease.

papers.abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is common, frequently symptomatic, and closely associated with conditions already prioritised by the UK National Health Service (NHS), including obesity, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, cardiovascular disease, and stroke. Previous estimates suggest that approximately 8 million UK adults aged 30-69 years could have OSA, although the proportion remaining undiagnosed is uncertain. Evidence supports treatment benefits for daytime sleepiness, symptom burden, quality of life, driving safety, and blood pressure in some patients, but not a consistent reduction in major cardiovascular events. UK data indicate long diagnostic waits, regional variation, and gaps in follow-up. A proportionate NHS response should prioritise targeted case-finding within existing chronic-disease pathways, access to validated home-based diagnostics, specialist capacity for complex disease, and sustained treatment support. Implementation should be phased and evaluated prospectively for clinical outcomes, equity, workforce requirements, affordability, and budget impact.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: A large and increasing number of people are forcibly displaced worldwide because of war, food insecurity, and other crises. Streptococcus pneumoniae likely causes a substantial health burden in crisis-affected populations. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) are widely used in routine immunisation programmes, including through the Essential Programme on Immunization (EPI) to protect against pneumococcal disease. They are typically administered as a three-dose schedule, either as three doses in early infancy or two doses in infancy followed by a booster at 9-18 months of age. However, PCVs are rarely used in humanitarian responses. We evaluated the potential impact of logistically feasible PCV campaigns in such settings. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a pneumococcal carriage, malnutrition, and social contact survey in a camp for displaced people near Hargeisa, Somaliland, to parameterise a transmission model accounting for migration. We projected the effect of PCV mass-vaccination campaigns using one or two doses and vaccinating children <1, 2, 5, 10, or 15 years (y) of age in the Somaliland camp and three different crisis settings. We found that a single-dose PCV campaign with high vaccine coverage in children <5 y or older can partially control vaccine-serotypes for up to 3 y, preventing 27% (95% CrI: 20, 34) of severe pneumococcal disease, defined as a composite of invasive pneumococcal disease and nonbacteraemic pneumonia, when vaccinating <5 y olds and 38% (95% CrI: 29, 46) when vaccinating <15 y olds. Expanded age eligibility is needed for comparable protection in settings with increased migration or more interaction with unvaccinated host populations. A campaign vaccinating <5 y olds is the most efficient use of PCV with 108 (95% CrI 77-162) vaccines needed to prevent one case of severe pneumococcal disease. Implementing such campaigns in displaced populations worldwide would require about 30 million doses in the next 5 y. Key limitations included sparse empirical data on PCV effectiveness and pneumococcal disease in humanitarian settings, and extrapolation of Somaliland carriage and contact patterns to other crisis settings. CONCLUSIONS: Single-dose mass-vaccination campaigns offer crisis-affected populations an effective, pragmatic immunisation strategy to deliver PCVs if routine EPI services have been disrupted.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To systematically review CT-based LAA% for emphysema quantification, explore the application of percentage low attenuation area (LAA% below -950HU), in comparison with visual emphysema scoring. METHODS: Following PRISMA-DTA guidelines, searches were conducted (01-01-1972 to 01-04-2026) in PubMed, Embase®, and Web of Science databases to identify English-language studies of adults ≥18 years with CT-quantified emphysema. Two independent readers screened titles, abstracts and full texts against predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria. Studies comparing LAA%-quantified emphysema with visual scores were included. RESULTS: 737 studies were reviewed, 5 (0.7%) met the eligibility criteria. These studies originated from Asia, Europe and the United States. LAA% cut-off values for emphysema varied: two studies used a 6% threshold, one used 5%, another used 1.5%, and one applied ordinal severity thresholds from 1% to 25%. Visual classification also differed, with three studies using the Fleischner Society system, one using a modified 3-point score, and another using the Goddard classification. Agreement between visual assessment and LAA%-based quantification was generally poor, with reported kappa values of 0.22 (n = 1,221), -0.06 (n = 200), and 0.48 (n = 98). Two studies further reported agreement based on sensitivity (86.8% and 58.0%) and specificity (84.2% and 39.0%). CONCLUSIONS: Based on limited evidence, substantial heterogeneity exists between visual assessment and LAA% quantification in emphysema. Discordance between visual and quantitative CT assessment likely reflects differences in diagnostic criteria and technical characteristics, highlighting the need for standardized reporting and methodology. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This systematic review provides a comprehensive comparison of visual scoring and LAA% metrics. It demonstrates limited agreement and substantial methodological heterogeneity of CT assessment of emphysema.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a devastating condition characterized by airflow limitation, inflammation, and structural lung damage. Metabolic dysregulation is recognized as a critical feature, but the key metabolic drivers remain unclear. This study identifies transaldolase1 (TALDO1) as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator in cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD pathogenesis. TALDO1 is markedly upregulated in airway epithelial cells by CS exposure. Elevated TALDO1 promotes mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas its genetic knockdown attenuates CS-induced lung function decline and pulmonary inflammation. Mechanistically, TALDO1 activation redirects tryptophan metabolism toward the kynurenine pathway, leading to L-kynurenine accumulation. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of this pathway significantly alleviates mitochondrial damage, while L-kynurenine supplementation exacerbates injury. Treatment with the IDO inhibitor Epacadostat ameliorates CS-induced lung impairment and inflammation in vivo. These findings define a TALDO1-kynurenine-mitochondrial injury axis linking airway epithelial metabolic reprogramming to COPD, providing translational evidence for targeting this pathway as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: Automated detection of pulmonary nodules on computed tomography has evolved from rule-based image processing algorithms to sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) systems capable of nodule localisation, volumetric measurement and malignancy risk stratification. Four landmark papers published between 1994 and 1999 established the computational foundations of this field, introducing grey-level thresholding, morphological feature extraction, neural networks and three-dimensional analysis as core detection principles. We provide an overview of these foundational studies and trace the subsequent evolution of AI-based nodule detection, from early computer-aided detection systems to modern deep learning frameworks evaluated in the context of lung cancer screening programmes.

papers.title_zh: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E status prior to COPD- or cardiovascular-related death: a nationwide study.
papers.title_en: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E status prior to COPD- or cardiovascular-related death: a nationwide study.
papers.authors: Guilleminault L, Mounié M, Sommet A, Costa N, Renoux A, Lafaurie M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Airways Unit, Department of Respiratory Immunology, Toulouse University Hospital, Toulouse, France.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: COPD is the third leading cause of death worldwide. However, little is known about the characteristics of patients who die from COPD. The aim of this study was to determine the relationship between change or persistence in Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E (GOLD-E) status over time and COPD- and cardiovascular (CV)-related death. METHODS: Patients with COPD were identified by International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes in the French national health insurance database. Patients who died from COPD or CV diseases between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2022 were matched with living COPD patients. We performed a case-control analysis to compare the impact of the change in GOLD-E status between two periods: 13-24 months (period 2 (2026)) and 0-12 months (period 1 (2025)) prior to death or the index date. RESULTS: A total of 500 673 COPD patients died during the study period. Of these, 67 250 died from COPD and 41 585 from CV events. Of the patients whose deaths were COPD related, the proportion of patients with GOLD-E 2026 status increased between the two periods (58.3% versus 79.2%), but decreased in their matched living controls (58.3% versus 36.9%). Of the patients with GOLD-E 2026 status during period 2, becoming and remaining GOLD-E 2026 within their final 12 months was associated with COPD-related death (odds ratios 5.40 (95% CI 5.03-5.79) and 4.16 (95% CI 3.87-4.48), respectively; p<0.0001). INTERPRETATION: These data demonstrate that being GOLD-E for 2 years in a row is associated with a high risk of COPD-related death, of the same magnitude as being GOLD-E for 1 year.

papers.title_zh: 铜绿假单胞菌泳动与IV型菌毛通过改变细菌-巨噬细胞物理接触调节吞噬摄取
papers.title_en: Swimming motility and type IV pili modulate phagocytosis by shaping physical interactions between Pseudomonas aeruginosa and macrophages.
papers.authors: Distler T, Tsai CN, Huang HY, Pellegrino A, Weimann A, Al-Mayyah Z, Meirelles LA, Floto RA et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Global Health Institute, School of Life Sciences, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Lausanne, Switzerland…
papers.authors_conclusion: Together, our results show that swimming motility and type IV pili shape physical interactions between bacteria and macrophages, thereby influencing phagocytic uptake.
papers.ai_note: 摘要全篇无任何量化数据（无效应量、百分比、CI、P值或重复次数），信息不足，无法评估效应大小与统计学稳健性；结论基于体外巨噬细胞模型与T3SS缺失减毒背景，向慢性肺感染体内场景外推的依据不足；ΔfliCΔpilT 杀伤减弱被作者标为'surprisingly attenuated'的探索性观察，且其机制（遭遇减少 vs 效应器 engagement 受损）作者自陈未能区分；临床分离株结果仅定性描述，无分组数值。
papers.abstract_en: During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how P. aeruginosa evades phagocytosis under conditions that resemble chronic infection. We use an attenuated mutant lacking a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which reduces macrophage killing, allowing us to isolate determinants of bacterial susceptibility to phagocytosis. Using transposon insertion sequencing (Tn-seq), we identify bacterial fitness factors under phagocytic selection. Our screen reveals that disruption of genes involved in swimming and twitching motility reduces uptake by macrophages. We find that defects in flagellar and type IV pili (T4P) function interfere with the physical interactions between bacteria and macrophages. Live-cell imaging shows that motility-deficient bacteria exhibit reduced surface accumulation and unstable attachment to macrophages, limiting their internalization. Clinical isolates with reduced swimming or twitching motility display similarly impaired uptake. We also test the influence of bacterial motility on macrophage survival by restoring T3SS activity in flagellar and T4P mutants. In the PAO1 background, most motility mutants retained the ability to kill macrophages indicating that cytotoxicity dominates bacteria-macrophage competition in the presence of a functional T3SS. However, the non-flagellated, hyper-piliated ΔfliCΔpilT mutant showed a surprisingly attenuated killing, which may reflect reduced bacterial encounters with macrophages, impaired engagement of cytotoxic effectors, or both. Together, our results show that swimming motility and type IV pili shape physical interactions between P. aeruginosa and macrophages, thereby influencing phagocytic uptake.

papers.title_zh: NHE1调控SuHx大鼠肺动脉平滑肌细胞凋亡抵抗：通过抑制p38通路的机制研究
papers.title_en: Na+/H+ Exchanger Isoform 1 Regulates Apoptosis Susceptibility in Pulmonary Arterial Smooth Muscle from the Sugen/Hypoxia model of Pulmonary Hypertension.
papers.authors: Andrade MR, Yun X, Croglio MP, Niedermeyer S, Jiang H, Philip N, Murray S, Munson M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Physiology, Johns Hopkins School of Medicine Baltimore, MD 21224.

papers.ai_note: 信息不足（摘要无n、效应量、CI或P值，结果无法量化）；'necessary and sufficient'的强结论仅基于离体细胞实验，缺乏SuHx体内验证；内部张力：EIPA（抑制NHE活性）恢复凋亡，但缺乏离子转导的NHE1突变体同样赋予凋亡抵抗，提示转运活性可能非必需，与NHE活性升高为关键机制的表述存在矛盾，摘要未解释。
papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is characterized by vascular remodeling driven in part by apoptosis-resistant pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). Na+/H+ exchanger isoform 1 (NHE1) regulates intracellular pH and plasma membrane cytoskeleton anchoring, but the role of NHE1 in PASMC apoptosis remains unclear. PASMCs were isolated from distal pulmonary arteries from control and Sugen/Hypoxia (SuHx) rats, a model of PH. NHE activity was measured via the ammonium pulse technique, protein via immunoblot, and apoptosis via Hoechst staining, Caspase-Glo® 3/7 Assay System and Annexin V/ propidium iodide immunofluorescence. NHE activity and NHE1 surface expression were increased in SuHx PASMCs compared to controls. Despite increased endoplasmic reticulum stress at baseline, SuHx PASMCs were resistant to apoptosis following hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) challenge. Inhibition of NHE activity with ethyl-isopropyl amiloride (EIPA) and NHE1 silencing with siRNA restored apoptosis in SuHx PASMCs. Conversely, NHE1 overexpression in control PASMCs conferred apoptosis resistance. Expression of mutant NHE1 constructs lacking ion translocation or ezrin binding also reduced H2O2-induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, H2O2 increased p38 phosphorylation (p-p38) in PASMCs from control, but not SuHx, rats, indicating impaired activation of this pro-apoptotic pathway. NHE1 suppression via EIPA or siRNA restored p-p38 in SuHx PASMCs, while overexpression of NHE1 (wild-type or mutants) suppressed p-p38 following apoptotic stimulation. Inhibition of p-p38 with SB203580 prevented the pro-apoptotic effect of EIPA, validating a role for p-p38 signaling in NHE1-mediated apoptosis resistance in SuHx PASMCs. These findings identify NHE1 as necessary and sufficient for PASMC apoptosis resistance in PH, by a mechanism involving suppression of p-p38.

papers.study_type: 单中心回顾性横断面研究 · CPET亚队列相关与多因素回归分析
papers.title_zh: ILD患者下肢相角与亚极量运动氧脉搏显著相关，提示肌肉质量或影响运动循环效率但未能证实因果
papers.title_en: Skeletal muscle quality as an independent associated factor of oxygen utilization efficiency in interstitial lung disease: a cardiopulmonary exercise testing study.
papers.authors: Kaneko K, Ishizaka M, Hara T, Chiba K, Takei K, Ishikawa F, Fujioka H, Sakamoto K et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Rehabilitation Technology, Japanese Red Cross Medical Center, 4-1-22 Hiroo, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, 150-8935, J…
papers.authors_conclusion: Lower-limb PhA is an independent associated factor of O2 pulse in patients with mild-to-moderate ILD. Given the cross-sectional and retrospective nature of this study, these findings do not establish causality but suggest that muscle quality may be a relevant clinical indicator that warrants further prospective and interventional investigation.
papers.ai_note: 样本量小（CPET亚队列仅35例，且为111例中的选择性子集，完成CPET者可能存在选择偏倚）；横断面设计，作者已承认不能推断因果，但标题与结论中"independent associated factor"仍易被误读为独立决定因素；结局为亚极量氧脉搏这一替代指标而非临床硬终点；模型仅校正3个混杂因素，未调整性别、BMI、合并症等；信息不足：摘要未给出PhA与氧脉搏的绝对值范围及各变量的回归系数CI
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) is associated with poor prognosis. Oxygen pulse (O2 pulse) reflects exercise circulatory efficiency, but its determinants at submaximal exercise remain unclear. Phase angle (PhA) has recently emerged as a surrogate marker of muscle quality. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between lower-limb PhA and submaximal O2 pulse at the ventilatory threshold (VT), which reflects daily physical activity independent of maximal volitional effort, in patients with ILD. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 111 patients with ILD enrolled in an educational hospitalization program (April 2024-March 2026). Among these, 35 patients completed cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Lower-limb PhA was assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis. The association between PhA and O2 pulse at VT was evaluated using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis adjusted for age, %FVC, and tricuspid regurgitation velocity (TRV). RESULTS: The analyzed CPET sub-cohort (n = 35) had a mean age of 69.0 ± 8.4 years, 74.2% male, and %FVC of 85.3 ± 18.1%. Lower-limb PhA was significantly correlated with O2 pulse at VT (r = 0.629, p < 0.001). In multiple regression analysis, PhA remained independently associated with O2 pulse (β = 0.748, p = 0.001), with a model R2 of 0.433. CONCLUSIONS: Lower-limb PhA is an independent associated factor of O2 pulse in patients with mild-to-moderate ILD. Given the cross-sectional and retrospective nature of this study, these findings do not establish causality but suggest that muscle quality may be a relevant clinical indicator that warrants further prospective and interventional investigation.

papers.study_type: 体外细胞实验+顺铂耐药同源移植瘤小鼠模型的临床前机制研究
papers.title_zh: 化瘀丸通过诱导铁死亡增强抗PD-1疗效治疗顺铂耐药食管鳞癌（临床前研究）
papers.title_en: Huayu Wan induces ferroptosis and enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in cisplatin-resistant esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhu T, Wang B, Wang H, Ding J, Xu Y, Xu J, Dong L, Wang X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Shaoxing People's Hospital, School of Medicine, Shaoxing University, Shaoxing, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: These findings suggest that HYW promotes ferroptosis through coordinated disruption of glutathione metabolism and NCOA4-associated ferritinophagy while enhancing antitumor immune responses in cisplatin-resistant ESCC.
papers.ai_note: 摘要通篇为定性描述（markedly inhibited、greater antitumor effects等），无任何效应量、CI或P值；无样本量、随机化、盲法信息；标题/摘要强调的'enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy'仅基于小鼠同源移植瘤，未见人体证据；化瘀丸为中药复方，具体成分与剂量未交代，可重复性存疑；'generally acceptable systemic tolerability'无具体毒性数据支持。信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: Cisplatin resistance remains a major therapeutic challenge in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Here, we investigated the antitumor effects and underlying mechanisms of Huayu Wan (HYW) in cisplatin-resistant ESCC. HYW markedly inhibited the growth of cisplatin-resistant human KYSE150 and murine mEC25 cells and induced a ferroptotic phenotype characterized by reactive oxygen species accumulation, increased intracellular iron, glutathione depletion, lipid peroxidation, and reduced GPX4 expression. Ferrostatin-1 partially reversed HYW-induced cytotoxicity. HYW also promoted immunogenic cell death-associated changes, including extracellular ATP and HMGB1 release and cell-surface calreticulin exposure. Mechanistically, HYW increased p53 expression and impaired the SLC7A11/GCLC-dependent cystine-glutathione antioxidant system, whereas GCLC overexpression and P53 inhibition partially restored redox homeostasis and cell survival. In parallel, HYW suppressed AKT-mTOR signaling and promoted NCOA4-associated ferritinophagy, as evidenced by increased NCOA4 and LC3-II and decreased FTH expression. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy and NCOA4 knockdown attenuated iron accumulation and HYW-induced cytotoxicity. In cisplatin-resistant syngeneic tumors, HYW suppressed tumor growth with generally acceptable systemic tolerability, enhanced ferroptosis- and immunogenic stress-associated changes, reduced PD-L1 expression, and increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Moreover, HYW combined with anti-PD-1 treatment produced greater antitumor effects than either monotherapy. These findings suggest that HYW promotes ferroptosis through coordinated disruption of glutathione metabolism and NCOA4-associated ferritinophagy while enhancing antitumor immune responses in cisplatin-resistant ESCC.

papers.study_type: 前瞻性观察性可行性研究 · 治疗前后诱导痰生物标志物与咳嗽结局关联分析
papers.title_zh: 慢性咳嗽患者诱导痰中ATP、CD39L1与腺苷测定的可行性及其与咳嗽结局的横断关联
papers.title_en: Feasibility of Measuring Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP), CD39L1, and Adenosine in the Airways of Patients with Chronic Cough.
papers.authors: Wahab M, Kum E, Diab N, Brister D, Singer R, Oliveira A, Hassan W, Beaudin S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medicine, McMaster University, Hamilton, ON, Canada.
papers.authors_conclusion: Purinergic biomarkers can be measured in induced sputum. Lower adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse cough outcomes in refractory chronic cough. Measurement of airway purinergic biomarkers may help identify neuronal dysfunction and support the development of targeted therapies for refractory chronic cough.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告任何效应量、95%CI或P值，相关性强弱与统计学显著性无法核实；未说明是否预先设定主要终点、是否做多重比较校正，难治性组的关联与两组间的交互检验未呈现，存在按亚组选择性报告风险。治疗后ATP显著下降但标志物变化与临床改善无关联，削弱其作为可治疗特征/疗效标志物的论证，而结论仍推广至'识别神经元功能障碍'和'支持靶向治疗开发'，从诱导痰嘌呤标志物推断神经元功能属机制外推。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Extracellular adenosine triphosphate contributes to cough hypersensitivity through purinergic signalling, but airway purinergic biomarkers have not been well characterized in chronic cough. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of measuring sputum adenosine triphosphate, adenosine, and CD39L1 and their relationship with cough outcomes. METHODS: In a prospective observational study, 100 adults with chronic cough were classified as chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis (n=45) or refractory chronic cough (n=55) and received guideline-based treatment. Induced sputum was collected before and after treatment. Biomarkers were quantified using bioluminescence and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays and compared with 24-hour cough frequency, cough-specific quality of life, and cough severity. RESULTS: Baseline biomarker concentrations were similar between groups. In refractory chronic cough, lower sputum adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse patient-reported cough outcomes, whereas no associations were observed in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis. Sputum adenosine triphosphate decreased following treatment in the overall cohort and in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis, while adenosine and CD39L1 remained unchanged. Changes in biomarkers were not associated with clinical improvement. CONCLUSION: Purinergic biomarkers can be measured in induced sputum. Lower adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse cough outcomes in refractory chronic cough. CLINICAL IMPLICATION: Measurement of airway purinergic biomarkers may help identify neuronal dysfunction and support the development of targeted therapies for refractory chronic cough. GOV ID: NCT04758351 CAPSULE SUMMARY: Sputum purinergic biomarkers can be measured in chronic cough and may identify neuronal dysfunction, supporting their potential as treatable traits and biomarkers for targeted therapies.

papers.title_zh: COPD出院后患者对家庭vs中心肺康复的选择与接受度：因对照组被弃用而降级为单组前后对照的实用RCT
papers.title_en: Patient choice and uptake of Home-based rehabilitation with Health coaching versus Center-based pulmonary rehabilitation after a COPD-related hospitalization.
papers.authors: Benzo R, Beenken M, Hoult J, Midthun W, Benzo M, Thomas B, Ulrich A, Clark M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Mindful Breathing Laboratory, Division of Pulmonary & CCM Medicine, Department of Medicine, Mayo Clinic, Phoenix, AZ; Ma…
papers.authors_conclusion: 当在COPD相关住院后提供康复场所选择时，家庭康复是患者的首选选项。持续1年的生活质量改善可能代表重获福祉和/或提供初级姑息治疗的机会。我们的结果可能对临床实践具有重要影响。
papers.ai_note: 原为比较性RCT，因选择臂145例中仅1例选中心康复而丧失对照，降级为单组前后对照——无法区分干预效果与急性加重住院后的自然恢复/回归均值，结论中的疗效表述缺乏对照支撑。仅15%（294/1,906）接受度、56%完成率提示明显选择偏倚，外推性受限；'家庭是患者首选'实质建立在1/145这一极端分布上。摘要未报告任何QoL或步数的具体效应量、CI，仅给p<0.01，信息不足。结论选择性强调偏好与1年持续获益，回避了比较性主要终点未能检验这一事实。
papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Adherence to center-based pulmonary rehabilitation after a COPD-related hospitalization-which improves all outcomes, including survival-is only 3%. Home-based programs have been proposed as a more feasible option, but they are not systematically offered, and patient preference is unknown. OBJECTIVES AND METHODS: This pragmatic randomized trial involving patients with COPD recently hospitalized for a COPD exacerbation, originally aimed to investigate the comparative effect two arms: The choice of a facilitated referral to a center-based outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program or a home-based program versus a home-based program on adherence to post-hospitalization rehabilitation and disease-specific QoL measured by the Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire. The trial aimed to investigate the patient's preference of home vs center-based rehabilitation in individuals randomized to the choice arm. Daily steps were measured by Actigraph ®.The asynchronous home-based program included weekly health coaching and daily monitoring of daily steps, symptoms, and a 20-minute daily flexibility-balance exercise routine. RESULTS: Of 1,906 patients approached, 294 (15%) were randomized and agreed to the rehabilitation options offered by the study arms (uptake); of those, 56% completed the 12-week intervention (adherence). Of the 145 randomized to the choice arm, only one patient chose center-based PR; therefore, both groups received the same intervention, and results are presented as a one-group (before-after) analysis. Compared with baseline, the home intervention significantly improved (p < 0.01) physical and emotional QoL (Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire) and increased daily steps beyond the minimal clinically important difference. Trajectory models adjusted for age, FEV1%, and mMRC (breathlessness) confirmed sustained improvements in QoL at 6 and 12 months from baseline. CONCLUSIONS: When offered a choice of rehabilitation setting after a COPD-related hospital admission for an exacerbation, home-based rehabilitation is patients' preferred option. Sustained quality-of-life improvements in 1 year may represent an opportunity to regain well-being and/or deliver primary palliative care. Our results may have important implications for clinical practice.

papers.study_type: 研究类型待评定（启发式模式）
papers.title_zh: Echinacoside inhibits ferroptosis and pyroptosis in ARDS through modulation of the KEAP1/NRF2/P62 signaling pathway.
papers.title_en: Echinacoside inhibits ferroptosis and pyroptosis in ARDS through modulation of the KEAP1/NRF2/P62 signaling pathway.
papers.authors: Su D, Li R, Deng G, Li J, Ren J, Gao Y, Zhang J, Han Z et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Critical Care Medicine, the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University, Xi'an, China; Departm…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains a life-threatening pulmonary condition with persistently high mortality rates. Echinacoside (ECH) is a natural compound that has shown protective effects in experimental acute lung injury; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects in ARDS remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to explore the potential mechanisms underlying the protective role of ECH in ARDS. METHODS: The protective effect of ECH on ARDS mice was evaluated. Subsequently, network pharmacology combined with RNA-sequencing was employed to identify mechanisms modulated by ECH. Finally, the mechanism of ECH on ARDS was verified in ARDS mice and mouse lung epithelial cells. RESULTS: ECH reduced the level of inflammatory response and alleviated lung injury in ARDS mice. Network pharmacology and RNA sequencing results suggested that its mechanism may be related to regulating inflammatory response, anti-oxidative stress, and inhibiting cell death. Further experiments indicated that ECH inhibited ferroptosis and pyroptosis, possibly through regulation of the KEAP1/NRF2 axis. Molecular dynamics, molecular docking, and protein-small molecule interaction verification demonstrated that ECH binds to the Kelch/DGR domain of KEAP1. CONCLUSIONS: ECH binds to KEAP1 and may interfere with the KEAP1-NRF2 interaction, thereby promoting NRF2 release, which subsequently suppresses cellular pyroptosis and ferroptosis, ultimately reducing inflammation and lung injury. These findings support further investigation of ECH as a potential strategy for ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: Asymptomatic tuberculosis is a major but incompletely defined manifestation of the tuberculosis disease spectrum and an important challenge for active case finding. It is best understood as a symptom-defined and method-dependent phenotype rather than a uniform biological stage. Individuals classified as asymptomatic may have minimal or extensive radiographic abnormalities, low or intermittent bacillary shedding, or clinically inapparent disease that remains stable, regresses, fluctuates, or progresses. Differences in terminology, symptom ascertainment, population risk and diagnostic intensity have therefore led to substantial variation in how asymptomatic or subclinical tuberculosis is recognized and interpreted across studies and programmes. This Review examines current and emerging approaches for diagnosing asymptomatic tuberculosis, with emphasis on the interaction between epidemiological risk, radiological detectability, microbiological confirmation and longitudinal follow-up. Symptom-based screening and passive case finding miss a substantial proportion of bacteriologically or radiographically evident tuberculosis. Conventional sputum-based testing is constrained by difficulty obtaining specimens, paucibacillary disease, intermittent shedding and imperfect sensitivity. Chest radiography and computer-aided detection can expand screening capacity and standardize triage, but they cannot independently establish disease activity or exclude tuberculosis. Computed tomography and positron emission tomography/computed tomography provide more sensitive characterization in selected settings, although their cost, accessibility and limited specificity preclude routine use. Non-sputum pathogen assays and host biomarkers are promising because they may reduce dependence on spontaneous sputum, but most remain insufficiently validated, and their incremental clinical or programmatic value over imaging-based triage and conventional confirmation remains uncertain. The diagnostic challenge of asymptomatic tuberculosis lies not simply in the absence of symptoms, but in the unstable boundary between infection, early disease, radiological abnormality, microbiological detectability and future risk. Clinical and public health practice should therefore move beyond single-test strategies toward staged, risk-stratified diagnostic pathways that integrate symptom ascertainment, exposure risk, imaging, confirmatory microbiology, enhanced specimen collection and longitudinal reassessment. Such pathways should be viewed as flexible clinical-programmatic frameworks for organizing diagnostic uncertainty, guiding multidisciplinary decisions and generating testable hypotheses, rather than as validated treatment algorithms.

papers.title_zh: Mycobacterium abscessus induces immune suppression in cystic fibrosis macrophages.
papers.title_en: Mycobacterium abscessus induces immune suppression in cystic fibrosis macrophages.
papers.authors: Hill PJ, Miller CJ, Rascon R, Clary G, Idosa AW, Gavrilin MA, McCoy KS, Amer AO et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Microbial Infection & Immunity, The Ohio State University, Columbus, OH, United States.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: People with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) are highly susceptible to chronic lung infections with Mycobacterium abscessus (MAB), a nontuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) that is intrinsically resistant to antibiotics. While macrophage dysfunction is recognized in CF, responses to MAB in primary human macrophages remain poorly defined. METHODS: We investigated the innate immune response to MAB using peripheral blood monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages from pwCF and healthy donors. Macrophages were infected with opsonized smooth (MAS) or rough (MAR) isolates of MAB morphotypes at low multiplicity of infection. After removal of extracellular bacteria, intracellular burden, oxidative burst, NOX2 activation, and cytokine production were assessed at 2- and 24-hours post-infection. RESULTS: MAB uptake was comparable across all groups and non-CF macrophages showed no difference in intracellular MAR or MAS at 24h. In contrast, CF macrophages harbored significantly more intracellular MAR at 24 hours, a phenotype recapitulated by CFTR knockdown in non-CF macrophages. MAB-infected CF macrophages demonstrated a significantly reduced oxidative burst and diminished NOX2 p47phox phosphorylation. Non-CF macrophages treated with CFTR inhibitor mimicked the reduced oxidative burst. CF macrophages also exhibited an altered cytokine response with significantly elevated IL-8 but decreased IL-1β relative to healthy macrophages. Notably, MAR-infected CF macrophages secreted significantly less TNF-α compared with non-CF macrophages and exhibited markedly reduced apoptosis compared with MAR-infected non-CF and MAS-infected CF macrophages. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that CF macrophages are intrinsically impaired in their ability to control the virulent rough MAB morphotype, highlighting a potential mechanism for persistent NTM infection in pwCF and underscoring the need for host-directed therapies.

papers.authors: Rukminiati Y, Pangaribuan L, Adam K, Muna F, Perwitasari D, Tobing KL, Wibowo H, Rahayu S et al.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity, lineage distribution, and genotypic resistance profiles of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates across the Indonesian archipelago using whole-genome sequencing. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using 1,281 analyzed MTB isolates derived from the 2017-2018 National Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Survey (DRS TB). Samples were screened via Xpert MTB/RIF and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing using the MGIT 960 system. Genomic DNA was extracted using the CTAB protocol. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) libraries were prepared using the Nextera XT DNA Library Preparation Kit (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA). Sequencing was performed on an Illumina MiSeq platform using the MiSeq Reagent Kit v3 (600 cycles), generating paired-end reads of 2 × 300 bp. To identify drug resistance-associated mutations and determine strain lineage/sub-lineages, raw sequencing reads were initially processed with Trimmomatic. The filtered reads were subsequently aligned to the Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv reference genome (ATCC 27294;NC_000962.3) using the MTBseq pipeline, which the BWA-MEM algorithm (v0.7.17) for sequence mapping. Variant calling was carried out with Samtools mpileup (v1.6). RESULTS: Four major MTB lineages were identified: Lineage 4 (43.1%) was dominant, followed by Lineage 2 (30.4%) and Lineage 1 (26.3%), while Lineage 3 was rare, with only 0.16% detected. At the sub-lineage level, L2.2.1 (18.5%), L1.2.1 (11.3%), and L4.1.2.1 (9.7%) were the most prevalent. Resistance to first-line drugs was the most frequent, primarily driven by mutations in the katG p.Ser315Thr (7.5%) and rpoB p.Ser450Leu (5%), conferring isoniazid and rifampicin resistance, respectively. Second-line resistance was highest for Fluoroquinolones (2.03%). Notably, four pre-XDR strains (0.31%) were identified and validated across Java-Bali and Sumatera, all harboring critical gyrA mutations and rpoB mutations (p.Asp435Tyr, p.Asn437Asp, p.Ser450Leu, and p.Ser450Trp). CONCLUSION: The study confirms a high prevalence of L2 and L4 in Indonesia. The identification of pre-XDR-TB isolates among the national survey samples highlights an urgent need for expanded molecular surveillance. While newer drugs like Bedaquiline remain effective, the presence of specific gyrA mutations underscores the necessity of integrating WGS into national TB control programs to proactively manage resistance and optimize treatment regimens.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Vagal sensory neurons that innervate the airways signal the detected noxious information to the brain to produce a perceptible sensation called urge-to-cough as well as reflex and behavioural coughing. Understanding the central neural mechanisms in regulating airway sensory processing is important for the development of more effective therapeutic options for conditions such as chronic cough. METHODS: In this pilot study, healthy volunteers (n=14) inhaled nebulised capsaicin at a personalised maximum concentration for induction of a strong level of urge-to-cough without coughing. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) was employed to directly detect regional neural activity changes in the brain accompanying capsaicin-evoked urge-to-cough sensations. RESULTS: The neural activity in delta and high gamma bands increased with an increase in capsaicin-evoked urge-to-cough in multiple higher order brain regions such as the insula, the cerebellum, the thalamus, the putamen and the brainstem areas, including the medullary nuclei where airway-innervating vagal sensory neurons are known to terminate. CONCLUSION: For the first time, we have established the feasibility and utility of MEG for examining the brain control of coughing. We show that the neural activity in delta and high gamma bands in multiple brain regions including medullary nuclei is involved in processing of urge-to-cough, confirming previous findings with functional magnetic resonance imaging.

papers.authors: Yang Y, Yao Z, Zhang Z, Yu M, Yao C, Jia L, Hua F

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pneumonia is one of the deadliest lower respiratory tract infections worldwide, and rapidly distinguishing bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonia, and normal chest radiographs is crucial for guiding precise medication and avoiding misdiagnosis. However, the imaging manifestations of bacterial and viral pneumonia on chest X-rays often overlap, and some normal chest X-rays may also show atypical changes. Clinical differentiation relies heavily on the expertise of senior physicians. In primary care or emergency settings where experienced radiologists are scarce, this can readily lead to diagnostic delays and antibiotic misuse, further exacerbating the risk of antimicrobial resistance and severe outcomes. METHODS: To address this challenge, this study proposes a lightweight network named FLIFuse. By adopting a parallel multi-branch architecture, the model thoroughly mines discriminative imaging features, substantially reducing computational overhead while maintaining high classification accuracy. This provides a technical solution that balances accuracy and efficiency for medical image analysis in resource-constrained environments. FLIFuse consists of three heterogeneous branches: an ExtraDW module that enhances local texture details, a Conv2Next module that captures global semantic structures, and an FLI Block that fuses multi-granularity information across different receptive fields to strengthen the response in critical regions. RESULTS: The model occupies only 33.43 M parameters and incurs a computational cost of 6.61 GFLOPs. On the public ChestXRay2017 dataset, FLIFuse achieves a three-class classification accuracy of 91.4% for normal, bacterial pneumonia, and viral pneumonia, outperforming several current state-of-the-art models and attaining extremely low resource consumption while ensuring diagnostic accuracy. In cross-domain tests on an external COVID-19 chest X-ray dataset and the Nerthus endoscopic image dataset, the model also exhibits stable transferability, demonstrating its potential for cross-domain adaptation across different medical imaging tasks. DISCUSSION: These results demonstrate that FLIFuse strikes a favorable balance between diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an efficient and lightweight model option for computer-aided interpretation of pneumonia imaging, and showing potential for translation into clinical auxiliary diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: A 27-year-old man with cystic fibrosis, prior liver transplantation for advanced cystic fibrosis related liver disease, tacrolimus immunosuppression, multidrug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, recurrent drug induced liver injury, and intolerance to elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor underwent matched bacteriophage therapy. Intravenous phages were administered at 109 plaque forming units per dose and nebulised phages at 5 × 109 plaque forming units per dose twice daily. Within two days, marked elevations in alanine transaminase, aspartate transaminase, alkaline phosphatase, and gamma glutamyl transferase developed, prompting treatment cessation. Peak alanine transaminase reached 494 U/L and alkaline phosphatase 527 U/L were observed, while bilirubin and coagulation parameters remained normal. Extensive investigation, including magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography and medication review, identified no alternative cause. Rechallenge with nebulised phage therapy alone resulted in recurrent liver enzyme elevation after eight days, again resolving following discontinuation. Temporal correlation was demonstrated between liver function test abnormalities and detection of phage DNA in serum and sputum. No bacteriophage neutralisation, bacterial DNAaemia, development of phage resistance, or significant bacterial genomic change was observed. Despite early cessation, lung function improved over the subsequent six months.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Allergic and type 2 (T2) inflammatory biomarkers are increasingly used to predict outcomes and guide treatment in asthma and COPD. The objective of this cross-sectional study was to determine the prevalence of allergic sensitisation and T2 biomarkers and their clinical associations among patients with diagnoses of asthma and/or COPD in NOVELTY, a large multinational, observational study. METHODS: Participants were enrolled from primary/specialist care, stratified by physician-assigned diagnosis and severity. We assessed fractional exhaled nitric oxide (≥25 ppb), blood eosinophils (≥300 cells·µL-1) and allergen-specific IgE sensitisation (≥0.35 kU·L-1 to any of 11 aeroallergens). Associations between biomarkers and clinical outcomes were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index and smoking status. RESULTS: Data for all biomarkers were available for 4352 participants (asthma: n=2194; asthma+COPD: n=633; COPD: n=1525). Overall, 63% participants had at least one positive biomarker (asthma: 77%; asthma+COPD: 60%; COPD: 45%); only 8%, 4% and 1% of participants, respectively, were positive for all three biomarkers. Women and current smokers were more likely to be triple-negative. Among participants with asthma, having more positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease, lower lung function and exacerbations. By contrast, in COPD, having no positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease and lower lung function. CONCLUSIONS: Allergic and T2 biomarkers are highly prevalent in asthma and asthma+COPD but less frequent in COPD. Their patterns show distinct associations, sometimes with opposite trends, across diagnostic groups, suggesting distinct underlying mechanisms that differ.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in Malawi. While diagnostic pathways are well established, less is known about how people experience repeated care-seeking and diagnostic uncertainty before receiving a TB diagnosis. OBJECTIVE: To explore pre-diagnostic TB experiences and care-seeking among adults with TB and caregivers of children with TB in urban Blantyre, Malawi. METHODS: We conducted in-depth interviews with 14 participants in urban Blantyre, Malawi (five male patients, five female patients, and four female caregivers acting as proxies for pediatric TB patients under 11 years). Data were coded deductively and inductively, then analyzed using a framework approach. Social Cognitive Theory informed the interview guide, and Candidacy Theory informed interpretation of access to TB investigation across multiple healthcare encounters. RESULTS: Participants described prolonged, distressing pre-diagnostic journeys, with early symptoms of TB frequently misattributed to malaria or minor respiratory conditions. As symptoms persisted, participants reported repeatedly seeking care, often attending health facilities multiple times before TB testing was initiated. These encounters did not provide immediate diagnostic resolution and represented participant-reported opportunities for earlier TB investigation. Participants' social networks shaped decision-making along the pathway, occasionally reinforcing misattribution but often prompting escalation to formal care. Repeated unresolved encounters imposed substantial economic burden on participants and their families, including loss of income, business disruption, and increased reliance on family support. CONCLUSION: In urban Malawi, participants described TB diagnostic pathways shaped by symptom uncertainty, social and material circumstances, and repeated healthcare encounters without timely diagnostic resolution. The findings highlight the potential value of reassessing persistent or worsening symptoms during repeat encounters. Strengthening such reassessment may support integrated, patient-centered TB care and reduce avoidable socioeconomic burden.

papers.abstract_en: Endobronchial carcinoid tumor rarely causes secondary spontaneous pneumothorax. We report a female in her 30s who reported progressive decline in her overall exercise tolerance with dyspnea on exertion and frequent upper respiratory infections (URIs) for 2 years presented for persistent spontaneous pneumothorax (SP). Initially, she presented to the emergency department (ED) for concerns of cough with mild hemoptysis and congestion for 2 weeks. She was found to have a small left-sided pneumothorax. She was admitted and treated for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Post-hospital follow-up showed a persistent pneumothorax unchanged in size. She was followed for weeks with serial chest X-rays, which later showed an increased size of the pneumothorax. She was admitted, and a chest tube was placed. Later, bronchoscopy was done, which showed near complete occlusion of the left mainstem bronchus by an endobronchial lesion. Pathology results showed a well-differentiated neuroendocrine grade 1 tumor consistent with carcinoid. She was successfully treated with tumor resection and photodynamic therapy (PDT). This case highlighted an unusual presentation of an endobronchial carcinoid tumor that requires further diagnostic workup with appropriate intervention.

papers.authors_conclusion: Atisine 和 podophyllotoxin 表现出显著抗肿瘤活性，并显示出与 IL-1R1 和 AR 良好的预测性相互作用，提示其作为双调节剂的潜力，值得进一步实验验证；其有希望的抗肿瘤谱得到强细胞毒性、良好的预测性蛋白-配体相互作用、可接受的药代动力学性质及多靶点网络药理学分析的支持；这些发现为进一步优化和体内验证、开发靶向炎症驱动与雄激素依赖性癌症的新型抗肿瘤药物提供初步基础

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate natural compounds derived from Aconitum heterophyllum (atisine, linoleic acid) and Podophyllum hexandrum (podophyllotoxin), as modulators of IL-1R1 and AR using integrated experimental and computational approaches. METHODS: Phytochemicals were extracted from tuberous roots of A. heterophyllum and fruits of P. hexandrum using Soxhlet extraction and isolated by TLC and column chromatography. Cytotoxicity and long-term antiproliferative effects were assessed using MTT and colony formation assays in A549 (lung) and LNCaP (prostate) cancer cell lines. Computational analyses included ADMET profiling, molecular docking against IL-1R1 (PDB: 1ITB) and AR (PDB: 2YHD), 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations, network pharmacology-based target and pathway enrichment analyses. RESULTS: Podophyllotoxin exhibited potent cytotoxicity with IC50 values of 0.04 µM in both A549 and LNCaP cells, outperforming doxorubicin, while atisine showed moderate activity (IC50: 2.1-2.3 µM). Linoleic acid displayed weak anticancer activity (IC50 >100 µM). Colony formation assays confirmed strong suppression of clonogenic survival by podophyllotoxin and a moderate inhibitory effect by atisine. Docking studies suggested favorable binding affinities (-8.1 to -5.9 kcal/mol), and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable protein-ligand complexes with low RMSD fluctuations. ADMET analysis supported favorable drug-likeness for atisine and podophyllotoxin. Network pharmacology identified 133 intersecting targets, with key hub genes including SRC, EGFR, and AKT1, enriched in PI3K-Akt and cancer-related signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: Atisine and podophyllotoxin exhibited significant anticancer activity and demonstrated favorable predicted interactions with the Interleukin-1 receptor type 1 (IL-1R1) and Androgen Receptor (AR), suggesting their potential as dual modulators that warrant further experimental validation. Their promising anticancer profile was supported by strong cytotoxicity, favorable predicted protein-ligand interactions, acceptable pharmacokinetic properties, and multitarget network pharmacology analyses. These findings provide a preliminary foundation for further optimization and in vivo validation toward the development of novel anticancer therapeutics targeting inflammation-driven and androgen-dependent cancers.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent pulmonary inflammation and tissue remodeling, yet the cellular states and regulatory mechanisms underlying monocyte functional heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Here, we generate a high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human respiratory system and identify a diverse monocyte functional landscape in healthy lungs containing a HSPA1B+ inflammatory monocytes state. This population exhibits enhanced inflammatory programs, cytokine and chemokine activity, and shows a distinct position within the inferred transcriptional landscape of the continuous monocyte functional spectrum. Cell-cell communication analysis further reveals that HSPA1B+ inflammatory monocytes function as active communication nodes within a stromal-immune-vascular network, integrating MIF, extracellular matrix, and immune-regulatory signals while mediating CXCL and adhesion-associated interactions with surrounding cellular compartments. Comparative analysis of COPD lung tissues and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrates selective enrichment of this inflammatory monocyte program in disease-associated environments, whereas peripheral blood monocytes from healthy individuals and COPD patients show limited representation of this state. Integrated transcriptomic and m6A regulator-associated analyses identify WTAP, a core component of the m6A methyltransferase complex, as a factor associated with the inflammatory monocytes program. WTAP silencing in inflammatory monocyte models suppresses pro-inflammatory mediators while enhancing interferon-response and antigen-presentation programs. Collectively, these findings define an inflammatory monocyte state landscape in the human respiratory system and identify a WTAP-associated transcriptional program linked to monocyte inflammatory activation and functional remodeling in COPD. This study provides new insights into the organization of pulmonary immune states and the potential regulatory mechanisms underlying chronic inflammatory regulation in COPD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with severe uncontrolled asthma (SUA) and a T2 eosinophilic phenotype exhibit variable response to biologic therapy (BT). Currently, accurate biomarkers predicting this response are lacking. We aimed to explore whether microRNA (miRNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) profiles in bronchial biopsies (BB) may help identify patients achieving a complete clinical response after 6 months of BT. AIMS: To explore whether BB miRNA and mRNA profiles may be associated with clinical response to BT in SUA population. METHODS: Thirty-four consecutive SUA patients with a T2 high phenotype were characterized and underwent bronchoscopy with BB before initiating anti-IL-5/5R BT. Clinical response was evaluated 6 months later. Both, miRNA and mRNA were extracted from BB, and their expression profiles were analyzed via microarrays. Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway analyses were performed to understand the biological functions and signaling pathways involved. RESULTS: After BT, 64% showed complete clinical response, 18% patients were non-responders, and 18% obtained a partial response. Comparing non-responders vs. responders showed 35 differentially expressed mRNAs, and 8 miRNAs in BB samples. Integrated analysis of miRNA and mRNA data suggested that three key genes (FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3) may be involved in asthma pathogenesis. CONCLUSIONS: Expression patterns between responders and non-responders to BT appeared to differ in BB of SUA patients, highlighting the involvement of multiple pathways related to airway inflammation and airway remodeling. Our results provide preliminary evidence suggesting that FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3 might be involved in the biological response to anti-IL-5/5R therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening respiratory condition characterized by uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction. Zang-Si-Wei Qingfei Mixture (ZSW) is a promising Tibetan herbal formula used clinically to alleviate pulmonary symptoms, yet its pharmacological targets and therapeutic pathways in ALI have not been fully explored. This study aims to identify the bioactive constituents of ZSW and elucidate their protective and therapeutic mechanisms in ALI. METHODS: ZSW's components were identified via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) previously and network pharmacology. Target affinity was evaluated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. In vivo, C57BL/6J mice with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI were used to evaluate the pretreatment and post-treatment effects of ZSW and its core component, Ellagic Acid (EA). In vitro, MLE-12 cells and the PI3K/mTOR dual inhibitor BEZ235 were utilized to investigate the role of PI3K/AKT signaling and NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis. RESULTS: EA was identified as ZSW's core bioactive constituent, demonstrating high binding stability with AKT1, PIK3CA, and PIK3R1. In vivo, ZSW and EA significantly attenuated lung histological damage, edema, and alveolar-capillary hyperpermeability. Both markedly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Mechanistically, ZSW and EA inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and were accompanied by decreased NLRP3 inflammasome-associated proteins (decreased NLRP3, ASC, and cleaved Caspase-1) and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis (decreased GSDMD-N and lactate dehydrogenase release). Notably, the 6-h post-LPS therapeutic model showed that both treatments effectively reversed established lung injury. CONCLUSION: ZSW and EA exert anti-inflammatory and lung-protective effects, accompanied by modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling and suppression of NLRP3 inflammasome-associated pyroptosis. This provides robust scientific evidence for ZSW's clinical application and highlights EA as a promising therapeutic candidate for acute inflammatory lung diseases.

papers.authors: Chen M, Zhang N, Wu Q, Cao Y, Zhang Z, Tang X, Zhao B, Zhu C et al.

papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，摘要未报告任何临床疗效或安全性数值，所有机制（HIF-1α/JAK2/STAT3、NF-κB、NLRP3、Nrf2/Keap1、Th17/Treg等）为通路层面的推断整合，属假说生成而非验证；'已确立的安全性'来源于既往其他适应症使用，不能外推至COVID-19高危人群的疗效；针对JN.1/KP.3等变异株的活性未见实验数据支持；与胸科肿瘤业务关联极弱。信息不足：摘要无样本量、对照、终点与统计学信息。；数值未经四元组核验
papers.abstract_en: The continuous emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., JN.1, KP.3) and the significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 in patients with rheumatic autoimmune diseases highlight an urgent unmet clinical need for dual-targeted therapeutics. Daphnetin (7,8-dihydroxycoumarin), a natural coumarin compound with a long history of clinical use in China, prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection by downregulating the viral entry receptor ACE2 through inhibition of HIF-1α and JAK2/STAT3 signaling. This review synthesizes the pleiotropic pharmacological mechanisms of daphnetin, including anti-inflammatory (NF-κB, JAK/STAT, NLRP3), antioxidant (Nrf2/Keap1), immunomodulatory (Th17/Treg balance), and mitochondrial protective pathways. These pathways are critically involved in the pathogenesis of both severe COVID-19 and rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We propose that daphnetin represents a novel "one agent, dual protection" strategy: it not only blocks viral entry by reducing ACE2 but also mitigates the hyperinflammatory and oxidative stress states that exacerbate both COVID-19 severity and rheumatic disease activity. Given its established safety, oral activity, and low cost, daphnetin is a promising candidate for clinical translation in high-risk comorbid populations. Key unresolved questions and future research directions are also discussed.
